Join our dynamic team as a part-time Student Support in the Release Management department, where you will play a vital role in ensuring the continuity and high availability of the Release Portal. Imagine contributing to ongoing software development and quality assurance within the Platform Engineering division in Denmark. You will focus on full-stack web application development and test automation integration, ensuring that new portal features are robustly built, thoroughly tested, and seamlessly deployed. Your work will directly support fleet maintenance readiness and portal stability, making a significant impact on our operations.

• Develop and implement new features for the Release Portal web application using C#, TypeScript, and JavaScript

• Collaborate with the Software Architect to design and write clean, maintainable code following SOLID principles and object-oriented design patterns

• Work closely with the Product Owner to refine requirements and break them down into actionable development tasks within an Agile/SAFe framework

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

jobs.occupation: Open-Rank Faculty Positions in Computer Science at Aarhus University, Denmark
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Center for the Theory of Inte
jobs.description:
Aarhus University - an international top 100 University - has made an ambitious strategic investment in expanding the Department of Computer Science. We expect to hire up to three candidates in 2027. Therefore, the department invites applications from candidates in computer science that are driven by excellence in research and teaching as well as a strong interest for innovation and addressing societal challenges.

The call is open rank, i.e. we are looking for tenure-track Assistant Professors, Associate Professors and Full Professors. The successful candidates will have a unique opportunity to shape the continued expansion of our computer science department.

The department consists of four Sections: Algorithms, Data and Artificial Intelligence (ADA); Cryptography and Cybersecurity (CRC); Human-Centered Computing (HCC); Programming Languages, Logic, and Software Security (PLS).

We are looking for applicants to strengthen and expand the above Sections, but topics beyond, or across sections are also welcome. We are, in particular, looking for applicants with competencies in the following topics:

• Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence
• Learning Theory
• Algorithms and Complexity
• NLP/Large Language Models,
• Generative Media Foundation Models
• Human-AI-Interaction
• Explainable and Trustworthy AI
• Data Management, Databases and Data Mining
• Economics and Computation
• Game Theory and Decision-Making
• Quantum Algorithms and Programming
• Software Engineering and Programming Languages
We generally encourage candidates within all areas of Computer Science – not restricted to the mentioned topics – to apply.

For full professorship candidates, we expect - in addition to excellent research and teaching in their field - that the candidates can demonstrate leadership, visions, collaborations and societal impact for the entire computer science department.

We provide starting packages with PhD funding (depending on position) and operational expenses for the first three years.

We wish to build a computer science research and study environment with equality and diversity as a core value for recruitment as well as for daily study and work life. If you have visions for or experience with activities or initiatives to support such core values in a computer science context, we encourage you to describe them in your application.

The starting date is flexible, from August 1st, 2027, and onwards.

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Åbogade 34, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Further information on the position can be obtained from Head of Department, Professor Kaj Grønbæk kgronbak@cs.au.dk.

About Department of Computer Science at Aarhus University

The Department of Computer Science is located in a developing campus area called IT-City Katrinebjerg, where many R&D institutions and companies within digital technologies are located. The Department has a staff of approximately 175 employees including 21 full professors (some part time) and 19 associate professors (some part time), 12 tenure track assistant professors, ~30 postdocs and ~70 PhD students, as well as 18 Tech and Admin Staff members. The student population is approximately 800. The Department’s ranking on CSRankings.org in the set of topics covered by the mentioned research groups is in top 30 in the World and top 5 in Europe. Read more about the Department of Computer Science on www.cs.au.dk

The benefits of working in Denmark

Denmark as a country offers the opportunity to pursue a career without compromising your family life and in general work-life balance in Denmark is among the best in Europe. In addition, Denmark is a safe place to live with a very low crime rate and is in general secure and equal. Denmark is considered in the top of the happiest countries in the world in international surveys. The Danish society builds on a welfare system which means your relatively high taxes goes into welfare services such as free healthcare and education. International academic staff members can usually also benefit from a special reduced tax scheme in the first years of employment. On top of this, collective agreements guarantee you a safe workplace, fair wages, pay during sickness, paid paternity/-maternity leave, flexible workhours and much more. If you want to know more about the Danish way of living please visit: Life in Denmark. Finally, Aarhus is assessed as the best study city in Denmark.

Natural Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Natural Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship position. 

The aim of the Natural Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Transformation Office Portfolio Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**The Senior Director, Transformation Office Portfolio Lead is a key role within Genmab’s Transformation Office (TO). The Senior Director will be the central orchestrator for operational and strategic initiatives, including initiative intake, prioritization, governance, reporting, and portfolio performance management. You will ensure that Genmab's most strategic initiatives are aligned with organizational priorities and deliver measurable business value. The initial focus of the Transformation Office is on R&D and Tech Ops (approximately 2,000 FTE), with potential for future scope expansion across the enterprise (⁓3,000 FTE).

The Transformation Office Portfolio Lead partners closely with senior business leaders, initiative sponsors, project managers, finance business partners and functional teams to drive rigorous initiative portfolio management, accelerate execution, and provide transparency on progress, risks, dependencies, and value realization.

As a key driver of the Transformation Office, the Senior Director will lead initiative portfolio management processes, develop recommendations on initiative prioritization, sequencing, and TO resource allocation, and ensure decisions are translated into action to maximize organizational impact.

The Senior Director, Transformation Office Portfolio Lead will report directly to Head of the Transformation Office (currently the SVP, Global Head of PPM & R&D Operations). The position can be located in Plainsboro, NJ, Utrecht, NL or Copenhagen, DK.

**Responsibilities

**

• Own portfolio management for cross-functional transformation initiatives that support Genmab’s financial commitments and strategic objectives

• Support the Transformation Office’s goals and objectives, aligned with the company’s overarching strategy and 2030 Vision

• Lead initiative intake screening, categorization, and prioritization processes, ensuring consistent application of prioritization criteria and governance framework

• Support, challenges and monitors projects, initiatives, and analyses focused on company transformation and productivity gains to inform strategic capital allocation and resourcing decisions

• Collaborate closely with Finance on Genmab’s long-range financial plan and annual budget cycle

• Drive the organization’s ongoing mindset shift toward productivity and prioritization

• Drive execution of initiatives from initiation through closure, ensuring clear ownership, milestones, and follow-through

• Track, report, and communicate TO initiatives to major stakeholders at all governance levels, including progress, risks, dependencies, and value realization

• Define, establish, and continuously monitor Transformation Office portfolio KPIs and success measures, ensuring transparent reporting of initiative performance, value realization, and overall portfolio health

• Lead the coordination and preparation of TO meetings and serve as meeting moderator

• Report on industry trends and peer company developments, translate their impact on Genmab, and improve overall strategic decision-making quality

• Work cross-functionally with R&D, Tech Ops, Commercialization, Finance, Human Resources, DD&AI, and other teams to drive alignment and execution

**Qualifications

****Qualifications and Requirements

**

• A minimum of 15 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree in life sciences, business administration, economics or finance required is required; advanced degree (Master's, PhD) preferred.

• Prior management consulting with direct biotech/pharma case experience advising clients on company transformations required

• Prior biotech/pharma operating experience in a Transformation Office capacity and/or program and project management with a Finance background also highly valued

**Requirements

**

• Passionate about life sciences and Genmab’s purpose and mission

• Demonstrated knowledge and expertise to drive company transformations and productivity initiatives

• Experience preparing executive-level materials and presenting recommendations to senior leadership and governance bodies

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills across the different levels within the organization

• Highly organized, attentive to detail, and results-driven, with a strong affinity for financial analysis, business performance metrics, and value realization

• Highly self-motivated, with the ability to take ownership, drive activities independently, and manage multiple priorities

• Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders, drive alignment, and achieve outcomes across cross-functional teams without direct authority

• Structured problem-solving skills

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK962.880,00---1.444.320,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology
jobs.description:
The Department of Forensic Medicine at Faculty of Health Sciences at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in the field of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology as per 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a permanent full time position.

As associate professor at the Department of Forensic Medicine, you will be part of a workplace with dedicated and specialised employees. The shared goal of our employees is to prevent and solve crimes, accidents, premature deaths and suicides through research, education and forensic examinations. The department is part of the Faculty of Health at Aarhus University with a permanent staff of seventy employees who work in two departments delivering impartial and evidence-based public sector consultancy for the danish police. The Section of Forensic Chemistry identifies and determines the purity of drugs in both biological material and illicit drugs seized by the police. The Section of Forensic Pathology and clinical forensic medicine performs forensic autopsies, crime scene investigations and clinical forensic examinations. Both departments hold either ISO 17025 or ISO 17020 quality standard accreditations. In addition to the two sections, the department has three research units which focus on bioanalytical chemistry, forensic imaging and clinical forensic medicine. The employees work in an interface between public sector consultancy and basic and applied research, and the department has particular focus on the good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for high quality in the performance of tasks at all levels. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As Associate Professor of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology, you will contribute to the department’s research, teaching environment and commissioned work, and to the university’s overall strategy. You will contribute to the development of the department both individually and in collaboration with others via your research of high international quality. You will furthermore contribute to the development of the department’s commissioned work within your area of expertise. You possess professional collaborative skills and a broad academic network across disciplines and institutions, which you are able to bring into play in your contribution to the academic development of Aarhus University and its profile both locally, nationally and internationally. 

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Commissioned work within the field of Forensic Anthropology
• Research of high international quality, including publication in top international journals and communicating your research in national and international academic networks.
• Teaching, supervision and examination of Bachelor’s and Master's degree students, as well as supervision of PhD students.
• Grant application to attract external research funding.
• Collaboration with relevant research environments across departments at Health, and with relevant national and international research environments.
• Involvement in assessment and committee work at Aarhus University.
• Dissemination of your research to the outside world.
• Contributing to the development of the faculty's PhD courses and new teaching activities

Your main teaching and research tasks, as listed above, may be conducted in affiliation with the Department of Molecular Medicine, Department of Clinical Medicine.

You will report to the Head of Department, Christian Lindholst, on matters relating to research and teaching, and to the Head of the Section of Forensic Pathology, Professor Lene Warner Boel, on matters relating to commissioned work.

Your competences 
You have established yourself as a prominent researcher within molecular bone histology and you possess documented solid research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. You have broad international cooperative partnerships, a documented ability to establish research collaboration across disciplinary and institutional boundaries, and experience of research partnerships with private and public-sector stakeholders, and you have potential of becoming a skilled group leader. At the same time, you have experience with grant writing to national and international funding bodies. We also draw attention to a stay or employment at at least one internationally recognised research institution. Finally, it is essential that you possess knowledge about forensic anthropological examinations, enabling you to actively contribute to the daily casework and develop the future of commissioned work within your area of expertise.

As a person, you are dedicated and a skilled communicator. You are able to build relationships based on trust with students, colleagues and partners. As a lecturer you communicate the newest and relevant knowledge in a committed, clear and comprehensible manner. As a supervisor you are professional, inspiring and inclusive.

You are ready to take co-responsibility for the development of the department's research, education and commissioned work at the highest international level and for ensuring that we maintain a good work environment. You naturally involve yourself in interdisciplinary collaboration at departmental, faculty and university level as well as nationally and internationally.

We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English. International applicants are expected to learn Danish, and Aarhus University arranges Danish teaching. 

In order to be assessed as qualified for an Associate Professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

Obtaining a child certificate is a prerequisite for employment in the position.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Head of Department Christian Lindholst tel.: (+45) 8716 7500

Your place of work will be the Department of Forensic Medicine, Palle Juul-Jensen’s Boulevard 43, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark. Teaching and research activities may also be conducted at Department of Molecular Medicine, Department of Clinical Medicine, Brendstrupgårdsvej 21A, 8200 Aarhus N.

Terms of employment
• Appointment as an associate professor requires research and teaching qualifications at the level that can be achieved through the satisfactory completion of a period of appointment as an assistant professor, but may also be obtained in other ways.
• The applicant is required to have completed a university pedagogical programme or an equivalent programme.
• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• The yearly base salary for a fulltime associate professor is DKK 706.233,06 (including a position related supplement, a pre-agreed associate professor supplememt and pension (18.07%)). Additional supplement(s) can be negotiated dependent on experience, special qualifications and performance of special functions. Authorisation supplement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.
• Researchers recruited from abroad are offered a special researcher tax scheme with a lower tax rate.
• Travel and moving expenses may be covered according to the employee in question and, to a limited extent, the accompanying family.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Application
Your application must include the following:

• Motivated application
• Curriculum Vitae
• Diploma
• Template for applicant - associate professor
• A list of publications
• A teaching portfolio. We refer to Guideline on the use of teaching portfolios
• The five publications stated as the most important in the 'Template for applicant - associate professor' must be submitted
• Research plan, which is part of the 'Template to applicant - associate professor' can be uploaded separately (optional)
• Coauthor statement(s) can be uploaded (optional)
• References/recommendations can be uploaded separately in the e-recruitment system (optional)
We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

International applicant?
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including assistance with relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about the International Staff Office and the range of services here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Job Title: Senior Director, Strategy & Corporate Development

Location: Brøndby, Denmark

Working model: Hybrid

Make an impact with us

At Milestone Systems, what you do matters. People are at the heart of everything we do, grounded in integrity, collaboration, strong relationships, and a curiosity that drives continuous learning. It is how we work together, learn from one another, embrace new perspectives, and create lasting impact.

In this role, you will help shape Milestone’s strategic direction and, equally importantly, turn strategy into action. jobs.occupation: Rethinking Converter Synchronization: 2-Year Postdoctoral Position in Battery Energy Storage Systems
jobs.description:
Are you eager to contribute to a bold experimental research project at the forefront of power electronics and energy storage? We are offering an exciting 2-year postdoctoral position for a talented researcher to investigate advanced converter synchronization and control methods for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with particular emphasis on exploiting naturally occurring acoustic and vibration information. The project combines converter control, sensing, signal processing, and experimental validation to explore new approaches toward simpler, more robust, and scalable BESS operation. This position is expected to start from 1st of January 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

About the project
The position is affiliated with the VILLUM Experiment project A-choir and the EMI/EMC In Power Electronics research group at AAU Energy. The project investigates new synchronization concepts for multi-converter BESSs by combining power electronics, sensing, signal processing, and control. A particular focus is placed on whether physical signatures naturally generated during converter operation can provide useful information for synchronization and coordination. 

You will join a research environment working across power electronics, EMI/EMC, converter control, multi-physics analysis, and experimental validation with applications including battery energy storage systems and other converter-dominated energy systems, with opportunities for collaboration across disciplines. The position also offers opportunities for international scientific exchange, participation in leading conferences, and may include research visits to relevant academic or industrial partners.

Your work tasks
You will:

• Develop and investigate synchronization and coordination methods for power electronic converters.
• Develop sensing and signal-processing methods for acoustic and vibration measurements.
• Establish and evaluate relationships between physical signatures and converter switching/operating behaviors.
• Implement and validate the developed methods using real-time control platforms, HIL, and experimental converter setups.
• Assess the proposed approaches under representative BESS operating conditions, including robustness to interference and multi-converter interactions.
• Contribute to the coordination of related research activities, and disseminate results through scientific publications, conferences, and project deliverables.
The position may also include a limited amount of teaching and supervision in areas related to your expertise.

Your competencies
We expect you to have:

• A PhD in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience in power electronics, power converter modelling and control, converter synchronization, signal processing, EMI/EMC, or related areas.
• Strong programming and experimental skills using DSP, MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, hardware-in-the-loop implementation or comparable tools.
• Experience with one or more relevant methods, such as synchronization and coordination control, digital signal processing, time-frequency analysis, data-driven modelling, or machine learning.
• Good knowledge of battery storage systems or multi-converter systems; experience with synchronization control, hierarchical control, hardware design, or AI-assisted signal would be an advantage.
• A strong scientific publication record appropriate to your career stage.
• The ability to conduct independent research, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate effectively with academic and industrial partners.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
You are not expected to be an expert in all technical areas covering power electronics, acoustic/vibration sensing, signal processing, or machine learning. Strong competence in power converter control and synchronization, together with solid experimental skills and the ability to work across sensing, EMI/EMC, and system-level interactions, is particularly important. We value scientific independence, critical thinking, strong experimental skills, and a rigorous approach to modelling, implementation, validation, and documentation.

Who we are
The position will be based in the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems” at Department of Energy in Aalborg University (AAU Energy). AAU Energy is an international research department at Aalborg University dedicated to developing clean and sustainable energy systems across electrical, thermal, and mechatronic energy technologies. We offer an interdisciplinary research environment, advanced laboratory facilities, and extensive collaboration with industry and academic partners. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg; this position is based at the Aalborg campus. Read more at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements 
Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma) 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.
• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc. 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position 
• References/recommendations 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society. 

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment. 

Do you have any questions? 
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.     

Further information 
Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Director

CMC Analysis & Characterisation

CMC Analytical Execution & Technology

Location: Måløv

Your impact begins here - **Set the direction. Accelerate delivery. Transform analytical execution.

**Are you a bold and inspiring leader who can turn complexity into clear direction and strong results? As Director of CMC Analytical Execution & Technology (AET), you will lead a multidisciplinary organisation of approximately 150 employees, ensure reliable analytical delivery across a growing development portfolio, and shape the future of automation, digitalisation, and analytical technology. This is an opportunity to combine visible operational leadership with strategic influence - and build the people, partnerships, and capabilities that will advance medicines from development to patients. Apply now and help shape the future of analytical execution.

**What You’ll Do

**As Director for CMC AET, you will lead a multi-disciplinary area consisting of five operational analytical teams, one IT team, and one Technology Engineering team. Together, these teams are responsible for delivering analytical results across the entire development project portfolio, while driving digitalization, automation, and technology advancement across the area. You will ensure reliable, compliant, and efficient operations through strong leadership, clear prioritization, robust resource planning, and close collaboration with key stakeholders.

At the same time, you will define and execute the strategic roadmap for analytical execution, digital capabilities, and technology innovation, ensuring scalable solutions and future-ready capabilities that support an expanding portfolio and increasing business complexity.

**Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

**

• Lead people and organisational capability: set a clear direction, develop leaders and talents, and build a high-performing organisation with the capabilities required to support current and future business needs.

• Drive performance and execution excellence: ensure reliable, compliant, and timely analytical delivery through strong operational leadership, clear accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement.

• Set strategic direction: define and drive the long-term strategy for analytical execution, validation, release readiness, and technology enablement, balancing business priorities, future capability needs, and regulatory expectations.

• Lead and build strategic partnerships: establish trusted stakeholder relations across the value chain and create alignment around priorities, capacity, risks, and resource investments to enable successful portfolio delivery.

• Shape the future through technology and innovation: define the vision and strategic direction for automation, digitalisation, and future ways of working across AnaC. Influence organisational priorities and investments to build the capabilities needed to meet future portfolio and business demands.

Your success requires a visible, hands-on operational leadership profile combined with strong strategic judgement. You stay close to execution performance, use KPIs and lead-time data to drive action, identify risks and constraints early, and work proactively with stakeholders to remove barriers and protect delivery. With full decision authority, you set objectives with significant functional impact and take accountability for people decisions, operational performance, strategic capability development, and successful project transfers from Research to Global Manufacturing & Supply.

You report to the Vice President (VP) of CMC Analysis & Characterisation (AnaC) and will be part of the leadership team in AnaC.

**Who You’ll Work With

**CMC AnaC is responsible for analytical development, characterisation, bioanalysis, stability, comparability, validation, release and lifecycle analytical support across Novo's product portfolio.

CMC AET consists of approximately 150 employees in Måløv, organised across five execution teams responsible for validation and QC/release testing, as well as a technology team and an IT team. The department is accountable for strong day-to-day analytical execution, predictable delivery, and transparent performance management, while strategically developing the automation, digital solutions, technologies, and capabilities required for the future analytical landscape.

We offer a dynamic and fast-paced environment where operational excellence, innovation, and collaboration go hand in hand. We take ownership, challenge the status quo, and are committed to delivering high-quality analytical support to patients and the business.

**What You’ll Bring

**We are looking for a seasoned and self‑motivated leader who thrives on taking initiative and ownership. You bring:

• An MSc (minimum) and + 5 years of relevant experience, with significant experience within QC, analytical development or other relevant CMC or Product Supply disciplines.

• + 5 years of proven leadership experience with the ability to lead multi‑disciplinary teams and deliver results at a strategic level. Senior leadership experience is a requirement.

• Broad cross‑functional experience within CMC Development, with strong organisational understanding and the ability to influence at VP level.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to present complex scientific and strategic topics to senior management.

• A demonstrated track record of driving change, challenging the status quo, and improving business outcomes.

• A strong Lean mindset and experience applying continuous improvement principles to simplify workflows, reduce lead times, improve capacity utilisation and build sustainable operational performance.

You lead with confidence, energy, and trust, creating clarity in complexity and belief in times of uncertainty. You set a strong tone of ownership and optimism - “we’ve got this” - and lead in line with Novo leadership behaviours by delivering on commitments, developing others, challenging constructively, and making decisions for the greater good.

**What You Can Expect Here

**At Novo, you can expect a role where your scientific judgement matters, your ideas are listened to, and your work helps move complex development projects forward. You will have opportunities to deepen your expertise, build cross-functional influence and grow in a collaborative environment where initiative is encouraged. You will be supported to perform at your best and trusted to take ownership, while contributing to work that helps create progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short‑term and/or long‑term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

We are looking for a Head of Retail to lead and grow Tekla's retail business as it accelerates internationally. This is a senior commercial role, with full responsibility for the performance, consistency, and growth of our stores, from the shop floor through to clienteling, retail marketing, and new store openings.

Reporting directly to the Commercial & Merchandising Director, you will have direct management and commercial responsibility for all owned stores, with real accountability for retail KPIs. You will work closely with partners managing stores in some markets, as well as our internal operations, marketing, and merchandising teams.

This is a unique opportunity to shape how Tekla scales retail. As our roll-out accelerates, new locations bring more complexity and a diverse mix of operating models. You will build the routines and standards that make this expansion consistent and commercially disciplined.

While our preferred location for this role is Copenhagen, we are also open to applications from candidates based in London. Please note that, in both cases, regular travel across stores and departments will be required.

Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Commercial performance and store management

• Hold direct management and full commercial responsibility for all owned stores and staffed department store spaces, currently Copenhagen and London, with a growing portfolio ahead.

• Extend the same commercial oversight to partner-operated locations, ensuring consistency in practice and driving performance even where day-to-day management sits with the partner.

• Own retail KPIs across every door, including revenue, conversion, footfall, AOV, and profitability, and manage each location towards its individual target.

• Build and embed weekly and monthly performance routines that drive both engagement and consistency across the retail portfolio.

• Lead, coach, and develop store teams, setting clear standards for service, engagement, and commercial performance.

Clienteling

• Lead and implement Tekla’s clienteling strategy across all stores, building the high-value customer base that underpins the retail model.

• Own the clienteling tool: adoption, daily workflows, and reporting.

• In collaboration with marketing, define and implement a clienteling calendar, to ensure high-value customers are engaged with in a meaningful way

• Define and track the clienteling KPI set, from appointments and outreach through to follow-up quality and revenue attribution.

• Ensure high-value client relationships are developed consistently, and to the same standard, across locations.

Retail marketing and activations

• In close collaboration with marketing, own the in-store events calendar as a primary driver of qualified traffic and brand engagement, spanning clienteling events, seasonal brand moments, and cultural programming.

• In collaboration with the PR & Community team, build local partnerships and community relationships in each market to generate reach, acquisition, and repeat engagement.

• Work with the trade team to ensure the stores are best leveraged as platforms to engage with architects and interior designers.

• Overall, use each store as a live platform for brand storytelling and customer acquisition, not only as a point of sale.

Store openings and expansion

• Coordinate store opening projects end-to-end, including site readiness, operational workflows, recruitment, and onboarding.

• Adapt the operating model to different setups, from HQ-managed to partner-operated and local-lead formats.

• Build scalable routines and playbooks so that each new opening is faster and more consistent than the last.

Retail operations

• Manage the retail operations function to ensure perfect synchronisation between the front and back end of the business, across stock, systems, POS, and fulfilment.

• Ensure consistency in tools, processes, and reporting across an increasingly complex, multi-format retail portfolio, and continuously sharpen our reporting to drive diagnosis and action across the network of stores.

• Partner with operations, technology, merchandising, and e-commerce to drive process and tool improvements as the business scales, and to deliver a seamless omnichannel experience for the customer.

We’d love to hear from you if you are/have:

• A retail leader with deep experience running stores, ideally across multiple regions or markets.

• Experience managing a clienteling tool and driving a clienteling strategy. This is essential to the role.

• A proven record of driving retail KPIs and building the performance routines that lift both engagement and results across multiple doors.

• Experience in retail marketing, including events, local partnerships, and activations that generate traffic and build the brand.

• Comfortable owning store opening projects, including recruitment and onboarding, across different operating models.

• Commercially disciplined and operationally strong, able to hold consistency across a portfolio of stores with different setups.

• Ideally, a premium or luxury retail background, with a genuine feel for service, experience, and brand representation.

• Genuinely drawn to Tekla's approach to product and brand; an appreciation for considered, quality home textiles matters.

If you have a genuine interest in connecting with clients through retail, an appreciation for Tekla’s approach and a commercial mindset, we encourage you to apply.

We are seeking a Financial Controller to own the integrity of Tekla’s financial reporting across the group. The role combines technical control work, balance sheet reconciliations, consolidation and eliminations, with ownership of a growing set of tax and trade compliance obligations spanning packaging tax, EU and global VAT and customs duties.

The Financial Controller is responsible both for meeting these obligations accurately and on time, and for building the processes, controls and automation that make them repeatable as the business scales. The role sits within an AI-first function focused on operational excellence, so we are looking for someone with a strong digital mindset and a proactive approach to using AI and automation tools to enhance reporting and improve efficiency.

This is a hands-on role, instrumental in ensuring financial accuracy and supporting Tekla's profitability and growth objectives. Reporting to the Finance Director and working closely with the Accounting Manager, the Financial Controller will also contribute to a range of ad hoc financial projects and initiatives across the function.

This is a full-time position based in our open-plan, curated office in Copenhagen.

Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Financial Controlling & Reporting

• Design, implement and manage the group's balance sheet reconciliations, including building standardised templates and processes across multiple entities

• Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and consolidated reporting packs

• Ensure the general ledger is supported by complete, reviewed and documented reconciliations in every period. While taking a hands-on approach to booking journals and ad hoc analysis.

Tax & Trade Compliance

• Own end-to-end packaging tax obligations, including data capture, calculation and filing

• Perform compliance reviews over packaging tax, taking a proactive approach as Tekla's global footprint grows

• Analyse customs and import duties, covering tariff classification, country of origin, preferential rates and duty paid versus duty due, and identify recovery and savings opportunities

Financial Analysis & Performance

• Monitor cash flow, working capital, and financial performance metrics

• Perform variance and accuracy analyses to validate forecasts, budgets, and data integrity, encouraging transparency and accountability

• Investigate material variances and implement process improvements that enhance forecasting precision and analytical rigour

• Provide insightful financial analysis to support business planning, cost efficiencies and strategic priorities

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support business objectives

Process Improvement & Automation

• Drive continuous improvement by leveraging AI and emerging technologies to enhance financial processes, systems, and reporting tools

• Support the automation programme within the accounting team, including Intrastat and VAT reporting

• Review and implement continual improvements in Business Central, including VAT code configuration, VAT statements and financial reports

• Strengthen documentation and controls across all owned processes so they are auditable and transferable

We'd love to hear from you if you are / have:

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field

• Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting standards and tax regulations

• Demonstrable experience of group consolidation and intercompany eliminations in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment

• Strong working knowledge of global VAT and sales tax concepts

• Exposure to packaging tax regimes is an advantage

• Experience designing and operating a balance sheet reconciliation control framework

• Confident ERP user, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

• Demonstrable experience using AI tools such as Claude to optimise and automate financial processes and reporting, for example building reporting dashboards, automating reconciliation and compliance workflows, or analysing large transactional data sets

• Advanced Excel skills and comfort working with large transactional data sets

• Experience from a high-growth business within fashion, textiles or luxury consumer goods is an advantage

• An entrepreneurial mindset with strong interpersonal skills

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English
